The actual fibers, including null ones, are a finite compatible family. The attainment and equality inputs produce a minimizing through-cap with a nonzero continuous normal, both endpoints on its boundary and both endpoints interior to positive fibers. Null-volume fibers may be dropped because every ambient halfspace retains exactly the same measured mass after their deletion.

Positively rescale the margin to continuous-normal norm one, preserving the closed cap. The lifted functional h has the two required endpoint values and takes values in [0,1] on all retained sections. Thus dist(h,[0,1]) is zero on every empty-side supporting section, including bases on either slab boundary. The full-side term is nonnegative and the proper-section term is strictly positive by an endpoint interior ball. In d=1 the proper trace has counting measure one. The flux inequality is impossible.

The original note f2d1fbdd5a877f5b has the declared archived digest. Section 3, second consequence, assumes precisely an affine base functional in [0,1] on every positive-volume base and uses the same zero exterior flux. Multiplication by the positive total mass converts its normalized depths to these raw depths without changing strict inequalities. The original proof uses the weaker flux inequality, and the stronger oriented version used here implies the same contradiction.

The original convex body contains every convex combination of the lifted fibers, which verifies compatibility. The projected base set is lattice complete since the projection of C contains the convex hull of those bases. Positive total mass and an own-fiber ball give a positive maximum, and positive-depth marks are precisely the own-fiber interior marks.

An actual minimizing nonvertical cap through the sampled interior segment point is already supplied by the accepted attainment fact. With two distinct sampled endpoints of positive depth and equality to their minimum depth, the cap passes through both and attains their common depth.

After null-volume fibers are dropped, the common cap and both interior endpoints meet the exact hypotheses. Choose the given base-affine h as an ambient affine functional and apply the inequality with positive proper-section mass and zero empty-side exterior flux.

overlap.comparison: Differentiable minimizing caps with a proper section have strict contact, which implies strict interpolation when the intermediate minimizing cap satisfies its derivative hypothesis. This slab theorem permits faceted supporting traces and uses orientation-resolved one-sided variation. Slab containment does not ensure two-sided differentiability.
